title: Learn to Look: Watch for When the Conversation Turns Crucial
coreMove: Shift attention from the topic to the conditions and name the exact silence or violence move as it starts.
sourcePressure: The reader must watch content and conditions at once, catching safety loss through silence or violence before the conversation is already flooded.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the chapter into a checklist of body-language clues.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

hook: dictionary definition of a crucial conversation
tryThisNow: pick a conversation and journal about it without a chapter-specific test
examples: manager feedback in a conference room
spouse argument at the kitchen counter
student raising hand in a classroom

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: telehealth therapy platform escalation chat between clinician support and engineering
exampleSpecs.audience: a support lead tracking both bug content and emotional conditions in text
exampleSpecs.stakes: a clinician outage may widen because masking in chat hides urgency until after clinics close
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the support lead sees three polite qualifiers in a row, labels masking in the side notes, and asks for the direct severity before engineering closes the ticket
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A chat window shows three typing bubbles and a red patient portal alert.

exampleSpecs.domain: commercial fishing boat crew debating whether to return before fog thickens
exampleSpecs.audience: a deckhand watching the captain and mechanic trade short phrases
exampleSpecs.stakes: weather risk grows while the crew avoids naming a faulty radar screen
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the deckhand notices everyone talking bait counts while looking at the blank radar, then names avoiding as the condition problem
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Wait," someone says, and a blank radar screen reflects a wet orange rain jacket.

exampleSpecs.domain: county library desk after a patron complaint about a banned display
exampleSpecs.audience: a branch manager trying to see when concern turns into labeling
exampleSpecs.stakes: staff may stop contributing because one patron gets reduced to a type instead of a concern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager hears a staffer say those people, marks it as labeling, and redirects to the actual request on the complaint card
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first signal is sensory before it is social: a complaint card sits under the barcode scanner beside a stack of returned novels.

exampleSpecs.domain: vascular clinic morning huddle where a medical assistant stops reporting delays
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic lead watching a usually precise assistant become too brief
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients may miss ultrasound slots because withdrawal hides the scheduling bottleneck
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead contrasts the assistant's normal detailed handoff with today's one-word answers and names withdrawal before the huddle moves on
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You notice a row of printed ultrasound labels curls in a plastic tray before anyone names the problem.

exampleSpecs.domain: indie game studio bug triage where a designer starts controlling the room
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer trying to keep bug severity discussion open
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may ship a broken tutorial because one loud voice forces meaning into the pool
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer catches the designer cutting off QA twice, names controlling as a condition issue, and pauses the content debate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Only later does the miss become obvious: a build number glows in the corner of a tutorial screen capture.

exampleSpecs.domain: farmers market vendor association deciding stall locations by email thread
exampleSpecs.audience: an association chair reading for violence and silence in asynchronous messages
exampleSpecs.stakes: a vendor may quit because sarcasm and avoidance distort the actual stall-access issue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair reviews the thread and highlights where masking became sarcasm and where two vendors withdrew completely
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes when a printed email thread is clipped to a clipboard beside a cash box?

skillTargets: track content and conditions at the same time
detect silence behaviors before they become full withdrawal
adapt the safety read to video, text, and in-person settings

tryThisNowSpec: During your next tense exchange, stop tracking the topic for ten seconds. Name the condition you see: masking, avoiding, withdrawing, controlling, labeling, or attacking.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
